chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Asadī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) went out one night after dark, while he was saying in a murmur: “A murmur, a dark night; the Imam has come out to you. Upon him is the shirt of Ādam, and in his hand are the ring of Sulaymān and the staff of Mūsā (عليه السلام).”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام), meaning Commander of the Faithful.
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The divinely designated leader mentioned here as appearing with prophetic signs.
key_terms.خَاتَمُ سُلَيْمَانَ: The ring of Sulaymān, a prophetic emblem of authority.
key_terms.عَتَمَةٍ: The darkness of night, indicating the late hour at which he emerged.
key_terms.عَصَا مُوسَى: The staff of Mūsā, a sign associated with prophetic power and miracle.
key_terms.قَمِيصُ آدَمَ: The shirt of Ādam, presented here as an inherited sign from a previous prophet.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the prophetic relics and signs possessed by the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration describes Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) emerging at night while uttering words that evoke the Imam’s connection to the inherited signs of the earlier prophets. It highlights continuity between the prophetic legacy and the authority of the Imam through symbols such as the shirt of Ādam, the ring of Sulaymān, and the staff of Mūsā.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abu Al Hassan Al Asady, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> went out one night after dark, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying, muttering, murmuring: ‘And the night is dark, the Imam<sup>asws</sup> has come out to you all! Upon him<sup>asws</sup> is the shirt of Adam<sup>as</sup>, and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand is a ring of Suleyman and a Staff of Musa<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from abu al-Hassan al-’Asadi from abu Basir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Amir al-Mu’mini (a.s.) once came out during the night after the ‘Isha’ prayer saying , ‘Ham hama, ham ham’and it is a dark night. The Imam (a.s.) has come out to you and he is wearing the shirt of Adam (a.s.). He wearing the ring of Solomon (a.s.) and in hands he has the Staff of Moses (a.s.).”
